apply: Not implemented. GoAI's inference surface is single-sequence: the batched GPU decoders (`llamagpu`) hold one device-resident KV cache per decoder, the analysis-path caches are per-model, and there is no request scheduler or continuous-batching engine that would consume a block table. Building the block-table machinery without that consumer would create exactly the orphan infrastructure the integration audits (§T444, §T519) exist to prevent. The single-sequence memory concerns PagedAttention incidentally touches are already served: bounded sliding-window caches with attention sinks (StreamGenerate), eviction policies (kvevict, SnapKV, PyramidKV), and an 8-bit quantized KV cache.

sum:
task tensor gatherCast: hoist innermost axis out of the strided-gather odometer — TARGET: gatherCast[S, D] in tensor/tensor.go (odometer at the loop containing idx[d]++ near line 210). It walks an N-D strided view element by element, paying a full nd-deep odometer tick per element: note: ALREADY DONE — no work performed this round, and that is the finding. gatherCast in tensor/tensor.go was strip-mined by commit 29eef4b8 (perf(tensor): hoist innermost axis out of the strided-gather odometer — 3.1x). The current source carries the hoist and its bit-identity rationale verbatim: inner, sInner := shape[nd-1], strides[nd-1], a straight strided run, and the odometer ticking over axes 0..nd-2. The task was complete but never archived, so it sat in the backlog as live work. Archiving it prevents a future session from re-deriving a shipped 3.1x optimization.

THE REMAINING tensor/tensor.go PS4005 SITE IS A DIFFERENT FUNCTION: gatherGeneric (around line 219), not gatherCast. Reachability was probed as this task mandated, by panicking inside it: NONE of BenchmarkCastF16toF32, CastF32toF16, CastBF16toF32, CastF32toF64, ContiguousOffsetView or ContiguousInnerRows enters it. Reading the dispatch shows why — it is the default arm for STRIDED CROSS-DTYPE HALF CASTS (the widen-through-f64 walk), so every same-dtype and every contiguous case is shadowed by gatherCast, gatherRows or gatherBlocked2D. It is reachable in principle (a sliced f16 view cast to f32) but no benchmark in the repo enters it, so its leverage is entirely unestablished. Carried forward as its own task with that evidence attached.

METHOD NOTE: the panic-probe step this task specified is what caught both facts cheaply. Reading the timing of a benchmark that never enters the function under test is the failure it guards against, and it would have produced a confident, meaningless number here.

A FIRST RUN WAS DISCARDED RATHER THAN REPORTED: its third rep had the control drifting +27% with both candidates rising alongside, which is exactly the discard condition this task specified. The reported figures come from a clean re-run. Recording this because the contaminated rep would have shown a WORSE result for the change and could equally have been mistaken for a regression.

REACHABILITY WAS PROVEN BEFORE ANY TIMING, and it was decisive: none of the six pre-existing candidate benchmarks enters gatherGeneric. Two new benchmarks build the shape that does — a sliced f16/bf16 [B,H,T,D] view materialized as f32/f64 — and were re-probed by panic to confirm entry. Timing any pre-existing benchmark would have produced a confident number about a function it never calls.

COVERAGE WAS PROBED, NOT ASSUMED: unlike autograd broadcastVJP (found completely ungated), this path IS gated — one existing test catches a broken strided walk. The added gate is stronger where it counts, byte-comparing against a frozen per-element oracle across the six S/D dtype pairs that reach here, INCLUDING the half dtypes: this path widens through float64 and f16/bf16 round-trips are lossy, so a change to WHEN the widening happens would surface only there. Both mutations turn it red.

NOT DONE, and it is probably the larger win: the per-element atF64/setF64 accessor dispatch, the PS1001 half. The modest 1.24x from removing the odometer alone is itself evidence that the accessor dispatch dominates what remains. It was kept separate because a typed switch creates a dual-path function (PS6001 applies) and must reproduce the widen-through-float64 semantics exactly, including the lossy half round-trips — a tolerance-0 cross-reference across every claimed dtype pair, with each arm mutation-probed, since a case named for an arm is not proof it reaches that arm. The oracle and benchmarks added here are the harness that work would need.

body:
Three research agents swept autograd, backend/ref and format/gguf. Outcomes.

SHIPPED. (1) nn.WKV exp elision: q is the max of its two arguments so half the four exponentials per element were computing exp(0), which is exactly 1. BenchmarkWKV 17.3 to 15.5 ms, -10.4 percent, two rounds interleaved in both orders, 9 samples per arm. Gated at exact bits against the unelided recurrence under two decay regimes so each side of the max wins in one. (2) backend/ref MoE-balance softmax computed each exp twice, once for the sum and once for the normalize; math.Exp is not inlined so the repeat was a second call. BenchmarkMoEBalance -34.06 percent F64 and -34.18 percent F32, confirmed in reverse order. This op has no CPU kernel, so the reference implementation is the hot path on every backend.

CORRECTNESS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: backend/ref MHAMaskedBackward took its four OUTPUT buffers from f64Data, an INPUT view that returns a detached widened copy for F32. Every F32 backward through the op returned four all-zero gradients, silently, so an F32 fine-tune of a trainable attention bias propagated nothing. It survived because every test touching the op built F64 tensors. Fixed via outF64 plus flush at both fast-path returns; regression floor asserts both non-zero AND agreement with the F64 run.

CHECKS ADDED. PS3018 was blind to every max-normalized pair before a REBINDING of the same name, since it kept only the last binding per name; bindings are now positional and the tree-wide count went 24 to 44. PS3027 input-view-on-output-tensor generalizes the F32 gradient defect: 4 findings pre-fix, 0 after, 0 elsewhere.

MEASURED AND REVERTED. The WKV elision in backend/cpu F32 (parallel scan): -0.9 percent pooled over 11 samples per arm, inside noise, because that scan fans across 12 workers and is no longer exp-bound. The autograd MoE division hoist: no movement, the loop is memory-bound across e separate slices.

NOT TAKEN, recorded for the next round. autograd: Cholesky VJP column-major layout for the four cubic loops (largest structural win found, n=512, all four loops walk columns of a [][]float64 whose rows are exactly one page apart); then parallelizing them with the in-package helper; the static-chunk deal in three parallel helpers versus the atomic cursor already used by the WKV VJP; and a triangle-only eigh Ab loop with no benchmark yet. format/gguf: ReadFile hands a bare os.File to the parser so every field is its own read syscall (about 160k for a 32k-vocab model), io.ReadAll grows a 638 MB data section at 1.25x, and the decode cursor claims tensors in file order rather than largest-first; the ReadFile benchmark currently SKIPS because models/ holds no gguf. Also a Q6_K dequant bounds check its two siblings already hoist, and a Quantize input copy that is pure waste for contiguous F32. backend/ref: SolveSPD substitution closure and stride-k walk, and a 16.7 MB per-call zeroed scratch in the masked attention backward that is fully overwritten before any read.

body:
Acted on two candidates recorded by the previous rounds research rather than opening new sweeps.

SHIPPED. (1) autograd Cholesky VJP: all four cubic loops read at least one operand down a column of a [][]float64 whose rows are exactly one page apart at n=512, so a column walk maps into a handful of L1 sets and misses on nearly every element. The intermediates are now built transposed (lT, lbarT, linvT solved directly in column-major, tmpT filled with j outermost) so each inner loop walks two contiguous runs; L stays row-major because the substitution reads it by row. BenchmarkCholeskyVJP_256 -26.2 percent (23.26 to 17.16 ms), _512 -22.0 percent (186.4 to 145.5 ms), median of 5 at 10 iterations. The trade is honest: two extra n-by-n intermediates cost about 17 percent more bytes and 257 more allocations at n=256. Gated by TestCholeskyVJPLayoutIsBitIdentical, which keeps the pre-relayout implementation verbatim as its reference and compares raw bits across n in 1,2,3,7,63,64,65,128; swapping a products operands stays green (IEEE multiplication is commutative) and reversing an index order reddens at n=2.

(2) backend/ref masked-attention backward: the per-head contribution buffer is heads*sq*sk float64, 16.7 MB at 8 heads and 512x512, freshly zeroed every call and fully overwritten before any read. Pooled it. B/op 25.2 to 11.8 MB, -53.2 percent; ns/op UNCHANGED and reported as unchanged, since a memset is a few percent of a body doing heads*sq*sk*dk MACs. The full-overwrite property is tested rather than asserted: poisoning every borrowed buffer with NaN leaves the suite green (direct evidence of full coverage) and deleting one column write reddens the reuse test.

CHECK ADDED. PS3028 unpooled-fully-overwritten-scratch: a scratch sized by three or more dimensions where every write is a plain assignment. Advice carries the resource framing (do not judge on ns/op) and the instruction to prove coverage by poisoning, because the scanner sees the shape of the writes and not their coverage. 1 finding pre-fix, 0 after, 10 advisory candidates elsewhere.

METHOD DEFECT FOUND AND CAST AS A RULE: the first before/after for PS3028 used git stash to get the pre-fix state, which also stashed the uncommitted detector and reported 0 findings — the check looked broken when it was fine. Restore the single FILE from git instead. Now BEFORE-AFTER-MUST-NOT-REVERT-THE-TOOL-001.

STILL OPEN from the previous sweeps: parallelizing the Cholesky VJPs four cubic loops with the in-package helper (do it now that the layout is fixed, since the column walks were memory-stall-bound and parallelizing first would have hidden the problem); the static-chunk deal in three autograd parallel helpers versus the atomic cursor; ref SolveSPD substitution closure and stride-k walk; and the whole format/gguf load path, which cannot be measured until models/ holds a gguf because BenchmarkReadFileModel skips.

body:
Two shipped, one of them only possible because a missing benchmark was written first.

(1) distillParallelRows now takes a newScratch function called ONCE PER WORKER and claims rows from a cursor. The previous round measured the cursor alone at -7.4 percent time with +26 percent bytes and +50 percent allocations and rejected it as a trade; moving the scratch out of the body turns the same transform into -16.6 percent and -14.1 percent in the two orders with allocations DOWN (56 to 46) and bytes flat. The penalty was never a cost of claiming, it was a cost of where the scratch lived.

(2) format/gguf ReadFile handed the bare os.File to the parser, so every header field was its own read syscall: a length then bytes for every string, and a llama-family header is dominated by the tokenizer arrays. BenchmarkReadFileSynth/header-heavy 66.0 to 5.5 ms, -91.7 percent; tensor-heavy 5.00 to 4.05 ms, -18.9 percent. Cost is 1.05 MB more per load, allocation COUNT unchanged.

THE BENCHMARK WAS THE BLOCKER AND IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE WORK. BenchmarkReadFileModel skips because it wants a checked-in tinyllama gguf the repository does not carry, so the entire load path had no instrumentation and every candidate from the format/gguf sweep was unmeasurable. BenchmarkReadFileSynth writes its own model into a temp directory. It has TWO shapes because the load has two independently sized halves — header cost scales with vocabulary and is constant in model size, decode cost scales with tensor bytes — and the same edit is 12x on one and 1.2x on the other, so a single shape would have hidden it. Its metadata carries a real tokenizer array for the same reason: every pre-existing benchmark in that package writes an empty metadata map, which is precisely why this cost was invisible for so long.

CHECK ADDED: PS3029 unbuffered-file-to-parser, with the constant-in-file-size property in the advice so the next reader knows a large-payload benchmark will not show it. 1 finding pre-fix, 0 after, 13 advisory candidates across every format package.

STILL OPEN, now measurable: the gguf sweeps other three candidates — sizing the data-section slab from Stat instead of io.ReadAll growth, claiming tensors largest-first instead of in file order, and the Q6_K dequant destination bounds check its two siblings already hoist. Also ref SolveSPD, and the ReadRaw per-tensor copy which still has no benchmark.

Two candidates from earlier sweeps, both measured and shipped.

(1) format/gguf Quantize materialized a full float32 copy of its input before handing it to an encoder. All eight encoders only READ that slice — verified before the change, no indexed write to the argument in any of them — so on the common path (a contiguous F32 tensor, which is what WriteQuantized feeds it) the copy was an allocation and a memmove of the whole tensor for nothing. BenchmarkQuantizeQ8_0 -9.6 percent time and -79.0 percent bytes; Q4_K -9.1 percent and -87.7 percent; allocations 2 to 1 on both. The read-only property is now LOAD-BEARING, not incidental: the alias is the callers storage, so an encoder writing its input would silently corrupt the tensor being saved. TestQuantizeDoesNotModifyInput pins it across every quant type and reddens when one encoder writes x[0].

(2) backend/ref SolveSPD ran both substitutions with the right-hand-side column index OUTERMOST, so every step jumped k elements through two buffers and re-fetched one factor element per innermost iteration. Making that index innermost walks two contiguous rows and makes the factor element loop-invariant. BenchmarkSolveSPD_64x16 -35.6 percent, medians of 6 at 500 iterations in both orders. OpSolveSPD has no CPU kernel so this reference implementation is the hot path, and its own VJP re-enters it.

THE KERNEL HAD NO TEST AT ALL, only benchmarks, which is why the bit-identity gate had to be written before the change could be trusted. TestSolveSPDInterchangeIsBitIdentical holds the pre-interchange nest verbatim, uses the kernels own Cholesky so the two differ in exactly one respect, and compares raw bits across shapes crossing k=1 (interchange is a no-op) and k>n.

DETECTION was already in place for the second one: PS6011 reported 3 findings on the pre-fix kernel and 0 after. What was missing was the remedy and its price, so the check now carries the interchange measurement and says why this shape is the cheapest of the class — the strided operand was indexed by an outer loop carrying no dependence, so interchange is two lines where the checks other two measurements came from relayouts.

STILL OPEN: largest-first tensor claiming in the gguf decode (needs a skewed-size benchmark, since the synthetic one builds uniform tensors); ReadRaw per-tensor copy (no benchmark); the ref eigh triangle-only Ab loop and the QR/SVD column walks (no benchmarks); vjp_cv poolAccessors per-element closures (no benchmark).

SHIPPED. Cast and Contiguous walked every view at its DECLARED rank. For the commonest shape here — a Slice on a non-innermost axis of a rank-4 attention tensor — that is thousands of short runs where a handful of long ones describe the identical traversal: on the packages own benchmark shape {4,6,64,64} over strides {32768,4096,64,1} the walk was 1536 runs of 64 elements, coalesced it is 4 runs of 24576. ContiguousInnerRows -11.9 percent, StridedCastBF16toF64 -7.7 percent, StridedCastF16toF32 -7.5 percent, ContiguousOffsetView -2.8 percent. An algorithmic gap rather than a constant-factor squeeze: the earlier campaign optimized the walk without asking how many axes it needed.

THE EARLY-OUT DECIDED THE SIGN. A first version allocated the folded shape and stride slices unconditionally; Contiguous and Cast run on every materialization and most views cannot fold, so those two allocations cost more than the walk they shortened — ContiguousOffsetView measured +18.4 percent. Scanning for a mergeable pair before allocating turned it into -2.8 percent. A per-call helper on a universal path must not allocate in the case it cannot help.

GATE: the property is checked against a per-element logical-index ORACLE, not against another implementation of the same idea, over 400 randomized shapes including permuted and sliced views where nothing may merge. Merging unconditionally reddens it.

THREE SWEEPS RETURNED and their unshipped candidates are recorded for later rounds. tensor: gatherHalfTyped carries a per-row closure, a loop-invariant branch tested per element, and a missing dst reslice (all absent from its sibling gatherCast); RoundToHalfF32 lacks a one-line dst reslice that would remove a per-element bounds check; the typed allocator free path re-boxes the slice header the typed path exists to remove, though nothing in production uses that allocator. Also a measured impossibility worth keeping: making AtF64 inlinable is out of reach — flatOffset alone costs 75 of the 80 budget, and three attempted restructurings all made it worse. classic: the presort split-finder gathers x[order[k]][f] across a 640 KB footprint (past L1) where a column-major buffer makes the hot column L1-resident; six static equal-chunk row loops; SVMs per-element non-inlinable kernel method call. rl and llamagpu: DQN.learn runs the same forward TWICE over the same batch with no optimizer step between; llamagpu headArgmax walks a [dim,vocab] weight matrix down columns and needs an in-package benchmark first.

ti: crossentropy scalar math.Log: call the existing vlogF32 (gated on PROC-007)
note:
CLOSED NO-ACTION on structural evidence; no benchmark needed and none run. The premise does not hold.

THE PREMISE: "backend/cpu/crossentropy.go:76 and :140 - math.Log running scalar in a loop", to be fixed by "CALL AN EXISTING HELPER" (vlogF32). Both halves are wrong at the code.

READ AT THE SOURCE, not from detector output. In the F32 forward the loop is over ROWS, and each iteration calls math.Log exactly once, on a single scalar:
    for i := lo; i < hi; i++ {
        row := zs[i*c : (i+1)*c : (i+1)*c]
        m := rowMaxF32(row)
        copy(scratch, row)
        sum := vexpRowF32(scratch, m)      // the c-wide per-element work, ALREADY vectorized
        lse := float64(m) + math.Log(float64(sum))
    }
The F64 forward (line 229) and both zl-branch backward sites (153, 304) have the identical shape: one log per row. The per-element transcendental in this kernel is the exp, and it is already routed through vexpRowF32.

TWO INDEPENDENT MISMATCHES with the proposed helper. (1) SHAPE: vlogF32(dst, src []float32) vectorizes a SLICE of logs; these sites have one scalar per row, so there is nothing to vectorize in place. (2) DTYPE: the call is math.Log(float64(sum)) - float64 - while vlogF32 is f32-only. The task asked to "confirm vlogF32's signature and dtype before assuming it drops in"; confirmed, and it does not drop in on either axis.

MAGNITUDE, to show the restructure is not worth attempting either. At the task's own benchmark shape 256x4096 the kernel evaluates 256 logs against 1048576 exps - the log is 1/4096 of the transcendental work. Batching the per-row sums into a b-length array to vlogF32 over them afterwards would vectorize 256 scalar logs at the cost of an extra pass and buffer. That is below any noise floor this repo has been able to resolve.

ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN-TREE, which is how this should have been caught before the task was written: both sites carry "//perfscan:ignore PS4002 math.Log one-per-row not per-element; c-wide exp already vexp'd".

PROCESS FINDING, second instance in two sessions. The other backlog item claiming the strongest remaining leverage - ADR-01KYJYY74VE27BSEH9VGZSNFMK on backend/cpu/attn_extra.go - also names a site that already carries a perfscan:ignore explaining why it is negligible, and measurement there confirmed the suppression (4.1 percent on one dtype of one kernel, R-01M01BZ0F1F3VVJVS2EAV73JBE). Both items were written from detector output without reading the suppression at the site. Cheap standing check before a detector-derived candidate becomes a task: grep the target line for perfscan:ignore and read the justification first - it costs one line and has now pre-empted two tasks.

NOT AFFECTED and left standing: the separately noted elementwise.go math.Erf sites, which the task already excluded as "write a vectorized Erf", a genuinely different job.

The PROC-007 gate this task waited on is in fact now clear (both nn ULP guards pass on main at 18589e1b), so this is closed on applicability, not on the numerics gate.

TARGET: backend/cpu/crossentropy.go:76 and :140 - math.Log running scalar in a loop. The file already calls vexpF32 and vexpRowF32, so the vectorized idiom is established locally, and vlogF32 / vlogQuadsNeonF32 are already in the configured vectorizedSiblingFuncs set. This is therefore CALL AN EXISTING HELPER, not write a new SIMD transcendental - a small change, which is what separates it from the PS4002 sites that would require authoring a vectorized primitive from scratch. Confirm vlogF32's signature and dtype before assuming it drops in; the crossentropy sites must be F32 for it to apply directly.

Also reported and NOT part of this task: backend/cpu/elementwise.go:273,:290 (math.Erf). No vectorized Erf exists in the configured set, so those sites mean "write one" - a materially larger job that should be judged separately.

GATED BY PROC-007/PROC-008. A vectorized log is a polynomial approximation, not math.Log, so this is NOT bit-identical - the same category the user just ruled on. Cross-entropy loss and its gradient are continuous outputs, so PROC-007 admits it in principle. But the standing gate applies: the two red nn ULP tests (TestGradFnBitIdenticalToSlowPath, TestEMAUpdateBitIdenticalToSlowPath) must be green first, so a deliberate approximation error does not land on top of an unexplained one and destroy attribution. Do not start until then.

WHEN UNBLOCKED, in this order:
1. Confirm entry: temporary panic at each math.Log site, run backend/cpu and nn tests, verify it fires. Do not read timings first - the AddBias lesson (benchmarks that name-match a feature but never reach it) and the gatherCast lesson both came from skipping this.
2. Establish the ERROR BOUND before the speed: compare vlogF32 against math.Log over the actual input domain of cross-entropy (probabilities in (0,1], where log is steepest near zero and worst-case relative error is largest). Report max ulp and max relative error. If the bound is not defensible near zero, reject - a loss that is wrong for confident-but-incorrect predictions is worse than a slow one.
3. Interleaved A/B, file-copy toggle, three alternations, medians, plus an unaffected control. Existing surfaces: BenchmarkCrossEntropyF32_256x4096_cpu and its backward twin; check they enter the changed branch per step 1.
4. Per PROC-008, replace any bit-identical assertion with a tolerance test whose bound is the one measured in step 2, and justify it in the commit. Prove non-vacuity by mutation, scoped to the test claiming the coverage.
5. Full-tree run to find every cross-path equality test the approximation disturbs - training-loop and reference-parity tests are the likely casualties.

NOT MEASURED: nothing was benchmarked, deliberately. Measuring before the numerics gate clears would invite shipping on a good number, which is the failure mode PROC-007 exists to prevent.

ti: Parallelise the SVC working-set scans and gradient update — the serial 74% that caps the fit at 1.35x
note:
CLOSED NO-ACTION on measurement. The direction this task proposed is real but does not pay at the sizes this scorecard uses, and I built it before concluding that rather than arguing it.

BUILT AND MEASURED. Banded working-set scans (both passes) plus a banded gradient update, with per-band partials combined in ascending band order. Swept the band count by varying the per-element work fed to the grain gate, interleaved with the serial form, arms alternating, first sample of each burst discarded, medians of five:

  n=1000   1 band 1.010x   7 bands 0.897x   12 bands 0.813x
  n=4000   3 bands 1.081x   7 bands 1.046x  12 bands 1.024x  (best: 5.19 -> 4.80 ms)

At n=1000 splitting COSTS up to 19 percent. At n=4000 the best split is worth 8 percent and decays as bands are added — the shape of dispatch overhead eating a shrinking chunk, not of parallel speedup. The existing classicBandGrain gate already returns 1 band at both sizes, so the current code is right at n=1000 and leaves ~8 percent at n=4000.

WHY IT DOES NOT PAY. The serial 74 percent is 3n element-visits per step, but n is only 4000 and each visit is a handful of compares — about 8 microseconds of work per pass. That is the same order as the cost of handing it out. Amdahl says the ceiling is 1.35x; reaching it requires the serial part to be big enough to split, and here it is not. The ceiling is real and unreachable BY FAN-OUT at these sizes.

REJECTED for 8 percent that only appears at one size, in a solver where a moved working-set choice has been measured at 1600x. Reopen if the scorecard geometry grows: the crossover is between n=1000 (loss) and n=4000 (small win), so at n=16000+ the split should pay properly and the gate would need a scan-specific work figure rather than the kernel-column one.

TWO METHOD NOTES WORTH MORE THAN THE RESULT.
1. The entry check earned its place immediately: smoBands(4000) returned 1 under the default grain, so the banded path never ran. Had I measured first, I would have "measured" the serial code twice and reported no change as a finding about parallelism.
2. The bit-identity test passed, and so did its MUTATION. Combining the pass-2 partials in DESCENDING band order — an equally valid argmin, and the failure the ordered combine exists to prevent — still produced a bit-identical fit. So ties do not arise in these fits and the ordering is not load-bearing here. Ascending remains the correct default, but the test does NOT verify that ordering matters, and no future work should cite it as if it did.

WHAT REMAINS. The ~1.9x per-core deficit against single-threaded libsvm (6.82 ms serial against 3.54 ms) is now the only path to the SVC_rbf scorecard loss, since fan-out is closed off. See R-01M05FYDNDE43.
sum: task Parallelise the SVC working-set scans and gradient update — the serial 74% that caps the fit at 1.35x — Parallelise the SERIAL 74% of the SVC RBF fit. Per R-01M05FYDNDE43, only the kernel column is parallelised today, which caps the whole fit at 1.35x with infinite cores; it already measures 1.31x, so nothing else in the current design can move it.
body:
Parallelise the SERIAL 74% of the SVC RBF fit. Per R-01M05FYDNDE43, only the kernel column is parallelised today, which caps the whole fit at 1.35x with infinite cores; it already measures 1.31x, so nothing else in the current design can move it.

TARGETS, in the SMO step loop (classic/svm.go):
1. Pass 1, the working-set scan: argmin of e over I_up and max of e over I_low, one O(n) sweep.
2. Pass 2, second-order selection of j over I_low, another O(n) sweep reading Ki[t] and diag[t].
3. The gradient update over all t after the two-variable sub-problem.
Per step that is 3n; at 79 steps and n=4000 it is ~948k element visits against 176k kernel evaluations.

BIT-IDENTITY IS THE HARD PART and is non-negotiable here: this package has measured that a 1.6e-7 kernel perturbation makes SMO run to maxIter instead of converging in 78 steps (1600x slower), so the working-set choice must not move.
- (3) is safe: one write per index, no reduction.
- (1) and (2) are REDUCTIONS. The serial loops take the LAST extremum on ties (`e[t] <= eUpMin`, `obj <= objMin`). A chunked reduction must combine partials in ASCENDING CHUNK ORDER with the same <= semantics to reproduce the identical index. Combining in completion order will silently pick a different, equally valid index and change the whole trajectory.
- The comparisons themselves are exact float compares, so no reassociation issue arises; only the tie-break order matters.

VERIFY, in this order:
1. Confirm entry with a temporary panic in each parallel band before trusting any timing.
2. Assert the STEP COUNT is unchanged at 79 and the digest of alpha is bit-identical to the serial fit, across several n and both classes' label encodings. A changed step count means the working set moved.
3. Interleaved A/B, arms alternating, first sample of each burst discarded, medians compared. n=1000 and n=4000.
4. Sweep GOMAXPROCS 1/2/4/12 and recompute the Amdahl fraction; it should rise well above 26.1%.

EXPECTED CEILING, so the result can be judged: removing the serial remainder entirely would take 6.82 ms toward ~1.5-2 ms on twelve cores, against scikit-learn's SINGLE-THREADED 3.54 ms. Note n=4000 gives each pass only ~8 microseconds of work, so per-dispatch overhead is a real risk at this size — size the fan-out to the work (SIZE-THE-FANOUT-TO-THE-WORK-001) and expect the n=1000 case to want a serial path.

NOT part of this task: the ~1.9x per-core deficit against libsvm (6.82 ms serial vs 3.54 ms). That is independent and neither change alone closes the 1.72x scorecard gap.

body:
DIAGNOSED. GoAI's quant kernels are bound by PER-WEIGHT PROCESSING, not by weight traffic. Observed, not inferred. Instrumentation reverted; nothing shipped.

METHOD. Sweep WEIGHT BYTES at fixed architecture — one 6-layer TinyLlama-shaped model quantized to five types — so op count, layer count and KV length are identical and only traffic changes. GPU time read from Metal's own GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime.

MEASURED, 16 generated tokens per point:
  fmt      MB   ms/token    GB/s   B/256w   bits/weight
  Q2_K  119.4       8.33    14.3       84          2.62
  Q4_K  204.7       6.06    33.8      144          4.50
  Q5_K  250.2       9.71    25.8      176          5.50
  Q6_K  298.5       6.58    45.4      210          6.56
  Q8_0  386.6       7.58    51.0      272          8.50

TIME DOES NOT TRACK BYTES. Q2_K reads the LEAST (119 MB) and takes the LONGEST (8.33 ms); Q8_0 reads 3.2x more and is faster. A bandwidth-bound kernel cannot behave this way, so the intended linear fit (slope = bandwidth, intercept = fixed work) is not applicable — the premise is refuted by the data rather than fitted.

THE PATTERN IS MONOTONIC IN BLOCK SIZE. Achieved bandwidth rises 14.3 -> 51.0 GB/s as bytes-per-256-weights rises 84 -> 272. The denser the packing, the WORSE the throughput. That is the signature of a cost paid per WEIGHT rather than per BYTE: every format decodes the same 256 weights per block, and the formats that spend more instructions doing it are slower regardless of how few bytes they read.

WHY THE EARLIER ALU PROBE MISSED IT. Removing ALL of Q3_K's unpacking arithmetic was worth at most 1.08x, which ruled out the shift-and-mask math. This result is consistent with that and sharper: the per-weight cost is not the arithmetic but the load/issue pattern — one byte-granular access per weight or per few weights, where llama.cpp reads wide vectors and unpacks in registers.

THE CHAIN IS NOW COMPLETE for the 7.14x gap to llama.cpp on TinyLlama-1.1B:
  host and synchronisation          12 percent of wall, ruled out
  submit batching                   already optimal at one command buffer per token
  attention and KV growth           2 percent at decode lengths, ruled out
  weight traffic                    NOT the bound — time does not scale with bytes
  per-weight processing in the      the residual, and the only candidate left standing
    quant matmul kernels

CANDIDATE FOR THE FIRST TIME WORTH NAMING: wide loads. GoAI's kernels index the weight blob as individual uchar/byte reads; the achieved-bandwidth ordering says the cost scales with how many such accesses each weight needs. Staging a block through uint4/float4 reads and unpacking in registers is the standard remedy and is what the ordering predicts would help. It remains UNPROBED, and four candidates in this campaign have died on probe, so it should be bounded before it is built — but unlike those four it is the residual of an elimination rather than a guess.

body: Context: M2 TinyLlama decode remains behind same-window llama.cpp at long context. Current split-K pass 1 is latency-bound rather than bandwidth- or compute-bound. Pair ownership (32 dimensions per lane) improved the leaf about 2.9x mainly through coalescing; quad ownership (16 dimensions per lane) then improved the leaf another 1.05x-1.18x. The rejected context-length autotuner P-01M065K8DWFBXS2V5DE5J8B7MP showed that isolated wins can reverse in real TinyLlama runs, so this proposal requires a production gate. No history entry tests the next geometrically adjacent layout. Scope: add an experimental lane-octet pass-1 kernel for sq=1, dk=64 in which eight adjacent lanes own one key and eight contiguous dimensions each; keep the shipped quad kernel and selector intact behind a test toggle until promotion gates pass. Correctness gate: compare octet output with quad and the reference across sk=8,128,512,1024,2048, GQA and MHA geometries; require finite output, max relative error within the existing f32 attention budget, and a deliberate selector mutation must fail. Performance gate: discard warmup; run 10 independent order-alternating leaf samples at sk=512,1024,2048 and require median octet/quad >=1.05 at at least two long-context cells with no cell below 0.98. Production gate: only if the leaf clears, run 10 alternating real TinyLlama Q4_K_M decode samples at ctx=8,512,1536; require identical argmax outputs, median >=1.02 at ctx=512 and ctx=1536, ctx=8 within 0.98, unchanged allocations, and each arm spread near 5 percent. Reject and revert the candidate if any gate fails. Record the generalizable layout result in jxsl13/perfscan.

sum: research M2 half-resident cached-f16 FFN is exact but only 1.0348x at the full leaf seam — The cross-projection cached-f16 FFN experiment was implemented and fully reverted after its first promotion gate failed. note: Consumed by the rejection of T-01M08R8SGSETD and P-01M08R4T1WEX9. body:
The cross-projection cached-f16 FFN experiment was implemented and fully reverted after its first promotion gate failed.

Implementation shape: convert the rows=64 normalized input f32->f16 once; run cached f16 gate and up through MPS; compute SwiGLU from half inputs in float and round directly to half; feed that half buffer into cached f16 down; convert only the final down output to f32. It did not concatenate weights, and the residual add remained outside the primitive.

Correctness was non-vacuous: a mixed Q4_K gate/up plus Q6_K down fixture used finite trained-like scales; every output was checked for NaN/Inf before error aggregation; the final f32 output matched the current cached-f16 sequence exactly (maxAbs=0, maxRel=0); disabling the selector made the capability decline the same supported shape.

Ten alternating warm Apple M2 samples, eight complete TinyLlama-shape FFNs per sample (M=64, D=2048, H=5632), measured baseline 1198.542 us versus half-resident 1158.206 us, only 1.0348x. Baseline/candidate ranges were 4.47%/4.76%. The predeclared 1.10x leaf gate therefore rejected the design before production benchmarking. All executable and test changes were reverted.

Learning: the removed conversion and elementwise passes are too small relative to three tuned MPS GEMMs to justify cross-language recorder/cache plumbing. Future GPU residency proposals should first measure or upper-bound the aggregate removable-pass share against their promotion threshold. Generalized as jxsl13/perfscan#758.

body:
Implement a Metal-only optional recorder fast path for plain quantized SwiGLU FFNs at rows>1. Reuse the existing persistent f16 weight cache; convert the normalized f32 input once; retain gate/up outputs and the SwiGLU result in half scratch; perform SwiGLU in float arithmetic while preserving the current half input/output rounding boundaries; run down directly from half; and convert only the final down result to f32 before the existing residual add. All unsupported formats, shapes, architectures, post-norm variants, and non-Metal recorders must retain the current path.

Verification: Q4_K/Q6_K mixed-weight parity against the current cached-f16 sequence with explicit NaN/Inf rejection; selector mutation proof; ten alternating warm TinyLlama-shape leaf samples at rows=64 requiring >=1.10x; ten alternating fresh-decoder TinyLlama Q4_K_M pp64 pairs requiring >=1.03x median, identical greedy argmax, finite logits, unchanged steady-state allocations; controls pp128/pp512/tg64 each >=0.98x. Fully revert executable changes if any promotion gate fails.

body:
Context: Current M2 TinyLlama Q4_K_M attribution shows pp64 at 1517.9 tok/s versus llama.cpp 1699.0 tok/s (1.1193x incumbent lead), while 97% of the GoAI per-layer GPU time is quantized matmul. The cached f16 route converts the same normalized input separately for gate and up, converts both half outputs to f32, executes f32 SwiGLU, and converts that result back to half for down.

Hypothesis: a Metal-only optional resident-FFN recorder capability can convert the normalized input once, run cached f16 gate and up MPS matmuls into half scratch, compute SwiGLU with half inputs and a half output using float arithmetic, feed that half output directly to cached f16 down MPS matmul, and convert only the final down result to f32. This preserves the existing half rounding boundaries without concatenating weights or changing portable fallbacks.

Prior rejection boundary: R-01M024DQCHEXH8PT2TATEE04H0 rejected an older standalone f16 chain because random weights overflowed half and its max-relative harness ignored NaN. This proposal must use trained-model values, reject NaN/Inf explicitly, and compare the fused path against the current cached-f16 chain. The rejected fused gate/up weight and strided chunk-expansion designs are not repeated.

Promotion gates on Apple M2: (1) exact or explicitly bounded finite parity for gate/up/SwiGLU/down outputs across Q4_K and Q6_K mixed blocks, with mutation proof that the production selector reaches the new path; (2) ten alternating warm leaf samples at TinyLlama rows=64 with stable spreads and at least 1.10x for the three-projection FFN sequence; (3) ten alternating fresh-decoder production pairs for TinyLlama pp64, identical greedy argmax and finite logits, at least 1.03x median speedup, no control cell pp128/pp512/tg64 below 0.98x, and unchanged steady-state allocations. If any gate fails, fully revert the executable experiment and archive the rejection evidence.

note: PASS: the proposal explicitly distinguishes the complete 64x32/K32 legacy geometry from the rejected dtype-only 32x32/K64 prototype, pins the exact incumbent commit and source hash, proves that M2 selects the legacy rather than tensor path, keeps production routing unchanged until a 1.10x leaf gate passes, includes live-path mutation and partial-tile correctness, and requires an alternating production comparison with decode controls. The main risk is translation error in the bank-aware staging layout; the declared partial-tile and trained-like parity cases expose it before timing.

Context: current merged main 90f774680445429abb342e5939868ffdaf645e1a measured 1537.3 tok/s at TinyLlama Q4_K_M pp64 in a fresh three-repetition run, while pinned llama.cpp b10450 commit ece963f41b0b02d7a0d61436ae365762c073a4c8 measured 1664.0 tok/s on the same model, host, f32 KV, FlashAttention off boundary. The robust prior five-pair campaign retained a 1.1193x incumbent advantage. Runtime capability output confirms Apple M2 Pro has simdgroup matrix multiplication but has_tensor=false, so the incumbent uses its legacy kernel_mul_mm_q4_K_f32 path rather than M5/A19 tensor operations.

Pinned source extraction: ggml-metal.metal SHA-256 9f70100ad5a2c487d10a84a2e25ff692b87572cb54db0a0ca40e6655e1d1d2ce. The complete legacy tile is 64 quantized output rows by 32 activation rows with K=32 steps, 128 threads in four simdgroups, 4096 bytes of half weight staging plus 2048 bytes of half activation staging on full tiles, eight float accumulator matrices per simdgroup, fused f32-to-half activation loading, Q4_K dequantization in 16-weight thread fragments, and direct device output for full tiles. Partial output tiles reuse 8192 bytes of threadgroup storage for a guarded float writeback.

This is not a replay of rejected P-01M08SN9PFECD. That attempt changed only operand dtype in GoAI's 32x32, K64, output-scratch prototype and reached 0.4018x the cached-f16 MPS production path. The incumbent couples half operands to twice the output-channel width, half the K step, a different bank-aware staging layout, twice the accumulator footprint, half as much activation staging per equal FMA work, and no full-tile output scratch. The experiment must port that complete geometry before drawing another conclusion about direct quantized matrix multiplication.

Implementation boundary: replace only the disabled qmatmul_q4k_mm experiment behind SetQ4KMatrixUnit for the first pass. Preserve the production selector and cached-f16 MPS route until all leaf gates pass. Adapt the pinned MIT-licensed algorithm to GoAI row-major X[M,K], Q4_K W[N,K], and O[M,N] without importing llama.cpp build infrastructure.

Promotion gates on Apple M2: (1) explicit selector reachability plus mutation proof; finite outputs and max relative error <=5e-4 against the current cached-f16 path on trained-like full and partial tiles including M9/N13, M33/N40, M64/N5632, and K multiples of 256; (2) ten alternating warm leaf samples at M64 K2048 N5632 requiring candidate >=1.10x cached-f16 MPS, plus M32/48/64/96/128/256 sweep with every routed shape >=0.98x; (3) only after leaf success, derive a shape gate and run ten alternating fresh-decoder TinyLlama pairs requiring pp64 >=1.03x, finite logits, identical greedy argmax, unchanged steady-state allocations, pp128 and pp512 each >=0.98x, and tg64 unchanged because M=1 remains on the cooperative path. Fully revert executable and test changes if any promotion gate fails; archive exact measurements and report any generalizable finding to jxsl13/perfscan.

body: At merged main 85584691 on Apple M2 Pro, the production TinyLlama Q4_K_M harness measures 173.7 tg64 tok/s and 1526.0 pp64 tok/s with three local repetitions. Source inspection proves StepNLast records the full transformer and final last-row head into one Recorder and calls Finish once, so pp64 already uses one Metal command buffer and one submit/wait. The retained encoder probe prices packing roughly 330 custom dispatches into shared encoders at about 0.9 percent under its least-contaminated estimate, below the leverage threshold. The retained pp64 leave-one-out chain matches the real M64 GPU duration to 0.05 percent and attributes about 97 percent to matrix multiplication. TinyLlama has 12 same-type fused QKV blocks and 10 mixed-type blocks with three projections; Metal does not enable fused gate/up after the measured fusion regression. With 22 output, 44 gate/up, 22 down, and one LM-head projection, this is roughly 131 cached-f16 quant projections. Each production projection separately converts f32 activations to f16, encodes one f16 MPSMatrixMultiplication, and converts f16 output to f32. Prior half-resident FFN and complete legacy Q4_K tile attempts were rejected, so the untested structural boundary is whether a shape-cached MPSGraph can absorb the two casts around each MPS matmul while remaining in the existing command buffer. The local macOS 26.5 MPSCommandBuffer.h is the defining API source and supports commandBufferWithCommandBuffer for wrapping an existing MTLCommandBuffer. This research is consumed by proposal P-01M08WKNGEF49.

body: Research R-01M08WMQ5MFDY is the consumed deliberation record. Current merged main 85584691 measures TinyLlama Q4_K_M pp64 at 1526.0 tok/s on Apple M2 Pro, while the pinned llama.cpp b10450 campaign remains about 1664-1699 tok/s under matched or shipping semantics. StepNLast already records the whole model into one command buffer, and the retained encoder-switch probe prices separate custom encoders below one percent, so another batching or encoder-packing refactor lacks ceiling. The remaining projection boundary is repeated roughly 131 times: cached Q4_K/Q6_K weights are f16, but every projection separately encodes f32-to-f16 activation conversion, MPSMatrixMultiplication with f16 output, then f16-to-f32 conversion. Test a shape-keyed cached MPSGraph that accepts f32 activations and cached f16 weights, casts and multiplies inside the graph, casts the result to f32, and encodes into the existing recorder command buffer through MPSCommandBuffer wrapping. This is distinct from the rejected half-resident FFN proposal, which changed a three-projection chain and reached only 1.0348x at its leaf, and from the rejected Q4_K legacy tile, which lost to the production cached-f16 route. The local macOS 26.5 SDK MPSCommandBuffer.h explicitly supports wrapping an existing MTLCommandBuffer; existing attention and convolution graph caches provide the repository pattern. Gates: production-equivalent Q4_K and Q6_K leaf parity with finite output and max normalized error no worse than 5e-4; ten alternating warmed samples after discarding first samples; at least 1.10x aggregate leaf throughput across TinyLlama M64 projection shapes and at least 1.03x full StepNLast pp64 throughput with decode no worse than 0.99x. If the leaf gate fails, fully revert without end-to-end promotion. If promoted, rerun the five-pair pinned llama.cpp campaign, preserve cache bounds and fallback behavior, and commit evidence. Any generalized benchmark or cache-key lesson must be filed on jxsl13/perfscan.

body:
Merged-main evidence at ca859046 leaves llama.cpp b10450 ahead by 1.1690x at pp64 after the f16-KV promotion. Existing attribution proves production prefill already uses one command buffer, encoder packing is below one percent, cached MPSGraph cast-matmul-cast fusion violates reduction semantics, and the legacy Q4_K tile loses to warmed cached-f16 MPS. The remaining measured structural seam is mixed-quant QKV: TinyLlama Q4_K_M fully fuses 12 of 22 blocks, but 10 blocks issue q, k, and v separately because q/k are Q4_K and v is Q6_K. The retained production-shape probe measures the current 12-fused/10-split projection stage at 6.311 ms for M64; an all-fused dense-f16 shape is 4.861 ms, 1.298x faster for that stage and predicts about 1.038x pp64.

Implement a Metal-only heterogeneous resident projection group. It SHALL retain the original raw quant segments for the existing M<24 decode kernels, but for eligible M>=24 it SHALL expand each segment with its original Q4_K/Q6_K semantics into disjoint columns of one combined f16 [K,Ntotal] matrix and encode one established MPSMatrixMultiplication. The output layout remains canonical q||k||v, so RoPE, cache append, attention, and every non-Metal backend remain unchanged. Do not requantize v, use MPSGraph, thread f16 through tensor, or allocate both separate and combined expanded caches.

Promotion gates: exact combined f16 expansion bytes against separately expanded Q4_K/Q4_K/Q6_K controls; finite output with exact parity against the established separate projection chain at M1, M64, and M512; timestamp labels proving grouped expansion/matmul execute and selector arms differ; combined expanded bytes no greater than the sum of the replaced expansions and enforcement of the existing cache budget; at least 1.10x for the mixed projection stage at M64 across ten interleaved samples; full trained TinyLlama pp64 at least 1.03x across three interleaved fresh-decoder campaigns, pp512 and tg64 no worse than 0.99x, unchanged greedy tokens, and stable controls. If promoted, rerun the pinned five-pair llama.cpp shipping campaign under PERF-015 and M2-INCUMBENT-ATTRIBUTION-HARNESS-001. Revert executable changes if any leverage, parity, memory, or fallback gate fails. Report every generalizable performance finding on jxsl13/perfscan.

body:
Merged-main evidence at caf5d7f4 leaves GoAI forward-only decode behind pinned llama.cpp b10450 by 1.083x under matched f16-KV semantics. The Q4_K and Q6_K M1 kernels are already near the M2 DRAM roofline, and prior attribution rejects encoder packing as sub-percent. TinyLlama Q4_K_M still splits q, k, and v in 10 of 22 blocks because q and k use Q4_K while v uses Q6_K; this costs three projection dispatches plus two RoPE dispatches per affected block. A noisy all-Q4 screen shows a 1.10x to 1.47x projection-stage upper bound, so the only candidate worth building is full heterogeneous fusion.

Add a Metal-only M1 QKV group specialized to raw Q4_K/Q4_K/Q6_K segments. It must consume the original resident quant bytes, preserve the established cooperative per-row arithmetic, produce canonical contiguous q||k||v output, then reuse one fused RoPE and the existing paired KV blit. This is distinct from the rejected f16-expanded M1 design: there is no f16 expansion, vendor GEMM, requantization, or altered reduction schedule. M>=24 keeps the current combined-f16 MPS path; M=2..23 and every other quant pattern keep their established fallback.

Promotion gates: bit-exact M1 segment output against three established raw kernels including ties, tails, and finite-value checks; selector coverage proving only Q4_K/Q4_K/Q6_K with aligned K and N enters the new path; no M1 combined-f16 cache fill; one grouped profile event with no MPS projection event; at least 1.10x across ten interleaved production-shape mixed-projection samples; trained TinyLlama exact greedy-token parity and checked-logit parity with tg64 at least 1.03x across three fresh-decoder interleaved campaigns, stable controls, and pp64/pp512 no regression relative to the existing grouped prefill path. If any gate fails, remove executable changes and archive the measured rejection. Pin all comparison baselines and report every generalizable finding on jxsl13/perfscan.

ti: Lower classic treeRadixCutoff from 512 to 32? It is worth 17.3 percent on the forest fit and changes which trees are grown.
note: compact
sum: adr Lower classic treeRadixCutoff from 512 to 32? It is worth 17.3 percent on the forest fit and changes which trees are grown. — Keep 512 - preserve the exact trees the frozen digest pins note: compact
body:
kind: radio
option: Keep 512 - preserve the exact trees the frozen digest pins
option: Lower to 32 and re-freeze the digest - accept different but equally valid trees for 17.3 percent
option: Lower only for classification, where the risk is smallest, and keep 512 for regression
choice: Keep 512 - preserve the exact trees the frozen digest pins
ctx: MEASURED, interleaved over three rounds: BenchmarkForestFit 123.3 to 101.9 ms, minus 17.3 percent, and the variance disappears - 101.9 ms every run at 32 against 123 to 144 ms at 512. TreeFit is flat. The comparison-sort path is about half the forest fit: radixByFeature is 50.7 percent of a parallel profile and its closure comparator, the pdqsort partition and the insertion sort are most of that. Cutoffs of 32 and 128 both land near 102 ms. THE COST: the bit-exact forest digest FAILS at 32, 64 and 128 and passes only at 512, so the change alters which trees are grown. WHY, AND THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM IN THE CODE: radixByFeature documented its unspecified tie order as irrelevant because thresholds sit between distinct values. That is wrong - the sweep skips a candidate cut when the gap between consecutive values is at most featureThreshold, a TOLERANCE of 1e-7, so values that are distinct yet closer than that behave like ties, and reordering them changes which pairs are adjacent and therefore which cuts are considered. Two sorts that disagree on those runs grow different trees. The comment has been corrected; no behavior was changed.
dec: Keep 512 - preserve the exact trees the frozen digest pins
cons: THE QUESTION WAS MALFORMED AND THE ANSWER IS BOTH OPTIONS AT ONCE. treeRadixCutoff was serving two callers with opposite cost profiles: a PER-NODE sort of a shrinking range in the CART builder, which wants a low cutoff, and a ONE-TIME presort of every row in the GBM builder, which wants a high one. Splitting it resolves the tradeoff instead of choosing a side. The GBM presort keeps 512 as the new gbmRadixCutoff - that is the option chosen here - and the CART per-node cutoff drops to 32. With the two separated: BenchmarkForestFit 121.5 to 101.3 ms, minus 16.6 percent with all three new runs below all three base runs; GBMFit flat at 66.5 to 64.0; and BOTH bit-exact digests pass UNCHANGED. The apparent model-behavior change was entirely the shared constant dragging the GBM presort along with the CART one, which also cost GBMFit about 25 percent. No trees change and nothing is re-frozen.

body:
Merged-main physical M2 profiling at f3332361 attributes 44 binary.add encoders to one TinyLlama Q4_K_M decode step: 317.958 microseconds of a 10.620541 millisecond command, or a measured 2.99 percent wall-time ceiling before considering scratch traffic. These are exactly the pre-norm attention-output and FFN-down residual epilogues. Their Q4_K/Q6_K projection kernels already compute the same f32 total that the following bounded BinaryN adds to dx. The prior rejected residual-add-plus-RMSNorm fusion changed the logit digest because it reordered more than the final addition; this proposal does not fuse normalization or alter reduction order.

Add a Metal-only optional QMatMulResidentAcc path for M=1 Q4_K and Q6_K cooperative kernels. It must write dx = dx + total in the lane-zero epilogue using the established f32 total, eliminate the separate scratch-target projection and BinaryN encoder, and leave ordinary QMatMulResident, M>1, every other quant type, post-norm/sandwich models, and non-Metal recorders unchanged. A narrow constructor seam must permit interleaved trained-model control and candidate arms without environment state.

Promotion gates: bit-exact output against established QMatMulResident followed by bounded BinaryN for Q4_K and Q6_K across production K/N shapes, nonzero initial destinations, tails, and finite-value checks; ordinary beta-zero Q4_K/Q6_K parity and median performance no worse than 0.99x; profile evidence proving each eligible epilogue emits one quant-acc event and zero binary.add events, with the production TinyLlama step reducing binary.add count from 44 to zero; at least 1.02x trained TinyLlama tg64 across three independent invocations of three fresh-decoder interleaved campaigns, exact checked logits and greedy tokens, stable controls, and pp64/pp512 no worse than 0.99x. If any exactness, fallback, ordinary-path, or end-to-end leverage gate fails, remove executable changes and preserve only the measured rejection. Pin the model and base commit and report every generalizable finding on jxsl13/perfscan.

body:
Context: Apple M2 Pro Q4_K M=1 decode is a retained cooperative leaf used by quantized LLM projections. Fresh 200 ms count=3 baselines after PR #1116 place real FFN shapes at roughly 278-304 us for K2048xN5632 and K5632xN2048. The kernel reads each aligned eight-byte q1/q2 span as four separate ushort elements for every output row and super-block. The Q4_K 144-byte super-block, row stride, and per-lane qs offsets are all multiples of eight, so an aligned ulong load can replace each four-load group without changing the GGUF layout or arithmetic order.

Hypothesis: load q1 and q2 once each as aligned ulong values, extract the same four ushort lanes in registers, and retain the existing float accumulation sequence. This is distinct from the rejected half-input Q4_K experiment, which changed operand precision, and from rejected raw mixed-QKV fusion, which improved an isolated leaf but missed its end-to-end gate.

Scope: add an independently selectable runtime-compiled cooperative candidate; preserve scalar and historical cooperative kernels. Route only M=1 shapes whose same-binary interleaved measurements prove a repeatable win. Apply the identical selector predicate to direct, resident, and Recorder paths. Do not alter Q4_K bytes, public tensor semantics, M>1 routing, unsupported-device fallback, or other quant types.

Gates: scalar, control, and candidate outputs must agree within the existing Q4_K numerical envelope, preserve finite/Inf/NaN classification, and leave inputs immutable. Benchmark identical resident buffers with AB/BA reversal, exclude one pipeline-transition dispatch, then time at least 32 steady-state dispatches per arm. Cover KV, square, mid-up, mid-down, gate/up, and down shapes. Promote only a contiguous measured M=1 region where every eligible shape reaches at least 1.10x median speedup in each of three independent count=7 campaigns; fallback controls must remain within 3%. Run full Metal and repository preflight validation. Record rejected variants and reproducible evidence. File any generalizable benchmark or packed-load finding on jxsl13/perfscan.

body:
CONTEXT: PR #703 already removed Storage.data any. The remaining scalar-access defect is the public wrapper boundary: Go 1.26.6 reports Tensor.flatOffset inline cost 75 and Storage.atF64 cost 67, but Tensor.AtF64 and Tensor.SetF64 cost 149 and 139, so every element pays two calls plus repeated field loads. Apple M2 Pro baselines over 4096 elements are 8.47 us for contiguous AtF64, 12.1-13.0 us for contiguous SetF64, and 8.48-8.74 us for strided AtF64.

CHANGE: specialize rank-1 and rank-2 public scalar access in one body so the common offset arithmetic and dtype arm are visible together. Keep rank mismatch, rank-N fallback, view offsets/strides, dtype conversions, half rounding, and panic behavior semantically unchanged. Evaluate F32 first; retain only changes that improve all declared common cells without regressing rank-N fallback outside noise.

GATES: add dtype-specific F32/F64/F16 access benchmarks and rank-1/rank-2/rank-N controls. Use three independent count-seven M2 campaigns, bit-exact cross-dtype/view tests, full tensor tests, race, pure-Go preflight, and final full CI. Report the general pattern of composable individually-inline helpers exceeding the caller budget to perfscan.

NON-GOALS: no storage-layout or allocator change, no unsafe indexing, no bounds-check removal that weakens panics, no bulk-kernel replacement, and no arithmetic reassociation.

body: Current production attribution on an M2 Pro records one whole TinyLlama Q4_K_M token in one command buffer but 340 separate encoders: 7.771 ms explicit encoder work spans a 9.268 ms command, leaving about 1.497 ms (16.2%) outside encoder busy time. The dominant Q4_K kernel already reaches about 185 GB/s on a 200 GB/s machine-level stream and exact Q4_K vector-load rewrites failed their leverage gate, so another arithmetic rewrite is not justified. Prototype a normal-recorder-only execution mode that retains one MTLComputeCommandEncoder across consecutive custom compute dispatches, inserts MTLBarrierScopeBuffers between dependent dispatches, closes it before blit or MPS boundaries and before commit/finish/free, and leaves the profiling recorder as one encoder per labeled event so attribution semantics stay stable. This changes execution structure without changing kernel arithmetic or public APIs. Validate exact logits and deterministic tokens, explicit dependency parity under buffer aliasing, lifecycle/error paths, and fresh-process production-shape M2 campaigns. Promotion requires a meaningful whole-token gain with no prefill or long-context regression; if barriers erase the gap, reject and remove the prototype. Retain portable backends unchanged. Prior-art/rejection inputs: PERF-M2-METAL-PROFILER-002, ADR-0019, R-01M08WMQ5MFDY8V704PG7Z81D4, P-01M0GVZY39F019H2V39YGZYT6S, and P-01M09G3PGREC4V2QG3P1RC6J1K.

body: Primary source: ggml-org/llama.cpp commit bb4caa7540188872173c44d161602d9271386413. ggml/src/ggml-common.h defines intermediate block_q8_K as float32 d, int8 qs[256], and int16 bsums[16], exactly 292 bytes. ggml/src/ggml-quants.c quantize_row_q8_K_ref scans each 256-value block for the signed value with largest absolute magnitude, uses iscale=-127/max, rounds each iscale*x with nearest_int, clamps the upper endpoint to 127, stores group-of-16 sums, and sets d=1/iscale; all-zero blocks store d=0 and zero quants. ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/arm/quants.c ggml_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_K decodes Q4_K scales/minima, uses Q8_K bsums for the affine minimum term, applies ARM int8 dot products to unpacked low/high nibbles, and combines integer sums with the Q4_K f16 scale times Q8_K d. The Q6_K sibling uses the same Q8_K activation layout. This is an approximate activation policy distinct from GoAI current exact F32 activation path. Port behavior from these pinned sources, retain exact mode as default, and record any deliberate divergence. The implementation research is consumed by the Q8_K primitive and opt-in decode tasks; no source code is copied without preserving repository license obligations.

body: Context: a pinned TinyLlama f16-KV xctrace capture is contaminated by 10.515 ms of foreign GPU overlap within an 18.720 ms command, so its Q4_K counters are directional only. The Q4_K stage nevertheless shows 47.72% ALU Limiter, 31.84% Buffer Read Limiter, and 9.05% Compute Occupancy while the cooperative kernel recomputes four ordered eight-value activation sums for every output-row pair. Proposal: for single-row Metal Q4_K decode with K divisible by 256, compute the exact lane-local float4 correction sums once into a compact device buffer and let ordinary Q4_K projections load them while preserving weight traversal, nibble arithmetic, simd_sum order, outputs, and portable fallbacks. First validation is backend-only and amortized: compare two ordinary K=2048,N=5632 projections in one command against one sum producer plus two sum-consuming projections in one command. Frozen gates: exact float bits for the produced ordered sums and output parity across K2048N2048, K2048N5632, K5632N2048 plus fallback shapes; 22 paired samples at count 7 in three independent campaigns; candidate/control median ratio at least 1.10 in the paired FFN leaf path; trained TinyLlama logits and greedy tokens unchanged; full f16-KV decode at contexts 8, 512, and 1536 improves at least 1.01 in every campaign. Measure producer and both consumers together. Reject and remove the route if any correctness or performance gate fails.

Production go:metal.mhaBackwardF32 currently loops over Batch and invokes c:mtl_mha_backward_mps once per sequence; each invocation allocates host-backed Metal buffers, creates a command buffer, commits, waits, and copies gradients. body: Research R-01M0RVG598FZA measured the fused depth-4 ViT stack at roughly 4.05 ms forward and 8.9 ms backward; backward rebuilds the full forward graph and dominates the approximately 9.7 ms complete training step. A correct Q/K/V grouping prototype reached only about 1.032x at the boundary and reversed in paired complete-step samples, so it is rejected. For recording-mode F32 Metal stacks only, materialize the expensive attention state and FFN pre-activations into a bounded two-slot native cache keyed by the forward output address. Backward consumes a matching entry once and uses a graph that reconstructs only cheap LayerNorm/GELU elementwise state; cache miss, eviction, repeated backward, unsupported shape, and eager inference use the existing recomputing path. Cap each retained state, serialize access under the existing Metal operation lock, retain no Go pointer, preserve exact logits/loss/all gradients/input immutability, and require at least 1.05x complete-step median with a 1.03x paired floor on the pinned M2 ViT workload.

note: Attribution completed. The fused depth-4 stack dominates the merged ViT training step; forward is about 4.05 ms and backward about 8.9 ms because backward rebuilds the forward graph. Q/K/V grouping was correct but about 1.032x at its boundary and unstable end-to-end. Bounded saved activations were correct but only 1.0156x complete-step after private buffers and upload pinning. Both executable prototypes were removed. Further work should avoid exporting dozens of MPSGraph intermediates and instead reduce backward math or fuse a wider training boundary.

ti: Implement and gate one-submission ViT LossAndGrad

note: Implements active proposal P-01M0RX1WNKETX under standing user authorization; promotion remains conditional on the research R-01M0RX17A7E98 correctness and performance gates.

Implemented portable ViT.LossAndGrad plus the optional Metal whole-objective capability. The supported F32 M2 path composes patch projection, all encoder blocks, mean cross-entropy, and all 56 parameter gradients into one cached MPSGraph command-buffer submission; unsupported geometry, dtype/layout, custom attention, or recorder state retains the private-tape fallback. Explicit encoder and patch VJPs avoid an MPSGraph automatic-differentiation abort at class-token concat/broadcast. Code commit 2f95fa87db1e5e9af037751dc2031488c08dc5b1. Exact binary SHA-256 4fa0f337813ef4b5eedfb0e4e3001eb7ccdcb5cd0014d21ab822bfcf28e22855. Three 7-sample, 20x paired M2 campaigns had medians 1.454x, 1.450x, and 1.499x; all-sample median 1.456x and floor 1.321x, clearing the 1.20x median and 1.10x floor gates. Portable and Metal numerical, ordering, immutability, recorder-isolation, preflight, and final Metal preflight gates pass. Evidence: internal/benchcompare/leadership/evidence/m2-metal-vit-loss-grad-20260824/. Generalized finding: https://github.com/jxsl13/perfscan/issues/876. The only full go test ./... failure was the reproduced unrelated nlp.TestDiffusionLMGrammarE2E assertion with no source overlap.

sum: adr Which M2 state boundary should own GPT AdamW updates? — A: explicit resident session with one objective-plus-AdamW command buffer note: Decision A is implemented and validated: explicit resident parameters, gradients, and F32 moments; one objective-plus-AdamW command buffer per step; explicit host synchronization and deterministic close.
body:
Choose among: A, retain parameters, F32 moments, and gradient buffers inside an explicit closable training session, encode the existing objective graph plus one in-place custom AdamW encoder in a single command buffer, and sync host parameters only explicitly; B, extend the objective graph with AdamW but continue uploading and downloading all parameters every step; C, keep LossAndGrad plus host AdamW and tune copies. Research R-01M0S55DWJFPQ measures steady native upload at 1.91 ms, gradient copy at 4.56 ms, Go result construction near 2 ms, and host AdamW near 10.5 ms, making only A capable of the declared torch leadership gate.
choice: A: explicit resident session with one objective-plus-AdamW command buffer
dec: A: explicit resident session with one objective-plus-AdamW command buffer
cons: The session makes stale host parameters explicit, requires Sync before external model use, owns deterministic Close semantics, uses F32 moment arithmetic matching the pinned incumbent, and must pass the internal 1.25x plus external 1.05x leadership gates. Per-step graph extensions that retain host copies and copy-only tuning are rejected.

body: Pinned primary source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/bb4caa7540188872173c44d161602d9271386413/ggml/src/ggml-metal, release v0.2.0. ggml-metal-impl.h defines N_R0_Q4_K=N_R0_Q6_K=2 and N_SG_Q4_K=N_SG_Q6_K=2. ggml-metal-device.cpp specializes FC_mul_mv_nsg=2; ggml-metal-ops.cpp dispatches ceil(N/4) groups of 64 threads. The official Q4_K and Q6_K kernels unconditionally process both rows inside every K/256 super-block and guard only final stores. Implemented the ARM64+GOEXPERIMENT=simd RBF kernel-column route by preserving scalar squared-distance accumulation, staging distances in the final column buffer, and batching ExpScaledF64 per band. Default, non-ARM64, and non-RBF routes remain unchanged. The exact implementation artifact won 6/7 order-alternated M2 Pro pairs and improved median end-to-end n4000_rbf fit from 5.048190 ms to 4.518638 ms (1.1536x), with median allocations unchanged at 1040; an earlier same-semantics campaign won 7/7 at 1.2218x. Same-binary controls measured 1.3078x at GOMAXPROCS=12 and 1.3785x at GOMAXPROCS=1. Scalar and SIMD fits both used 79 SMO steps and 42 support vectors, decision signs matched, maximum decision delta was 3.3306690738754696e-15, and repeated SIMD fits were bit-deterministic. Default and SIMD compiled-binary classic suites, full repository short tests, vet, and cross-build gates passed except the documented pre-existing linux/amd64 local archsimd-toolchain limitation. Continuous unrelated host load limits the claim to paired internal improvement. The candidate remains 1.3006x behind scikit-learn 1.9.0 on the identical cell (4.71 versus 3.621500 ms), leaving batched/decomposition SMO open. Evidence is in internal/benchcompare/leadership/evidence/m2-svc-rbf-exp-20260824; the generalized opportunity is perfscan issue #899.

body:
## Context
IQ2_XXS and IQ2_XS are distinct GGUF wire formats, but both decode each 8-value group through a fixed E8-derived grid and the same seven-bit sign parity scheme. Their M2 decode kernels need persistent immutable lookup data, identical one-SIMD-group-per-output scheduling, and the same direct/resident/recorder lifecycle. Duplicating residency and initialization would enlarge the correctness surface and initialization cost.

## Decision
Use one IQ2-family Metal infrastructure with separate immutable codebook buffers, type-specific block parsers, independent cooperative toggles, and independent benchmark verdicts.

The Go side reconstructs both codebooks from the public exact GGUF decoder rather than duplicating literal tables. The C/Objective-C bridge owns process-lifetime Metal buffers. Every direct, resident, and recorder path calls the same readiness guard and the same per-type cooperative predicate. The scalar kernel remains callable as an in-process control.

Model-loader admission is additive for exact GGUF wire types 16 and 17. It does not imply generic synchronous host offload: the fused ARM64 CPU route remains the fallback unless every required host cell clears the 1.10x gate.

## Consequences
Shared algebra and lifecycle have one implementation, while a regression or weak result in either wire format cannot promote the other. Persistent lookup residency removes repeated uploads from the hot path. The design extends naturally to IQ2_S only after its different block structure receives its own measured proposal.

## Alternatives rejected
Duplicated per-format residency was rejected because it repeats initialization and dispatch invariants. Literal shader codebooks were rejected because they create a second numerical truth source. A single family-wide promotion flag was rejected because one format could hide a losing cell in the other.
choice: Use one IQ2-family Metal infrastructure with exact decoder-derived immutable codebooks, shared readiness and residency, type-specific block parsers, independent cooperative selectors, and independent benchmark promotion.
dec: Use one IQ2-family Metal infrastructure with exact decoder-derived immutable codebooks, shared readiness and residency, type-specific block parsers, independent cooperative selectors, and independent benchmark promotion.
cons: Current main implements the decision through ensureIQ2Grid, format-specific upload routines, shared uploadResident dispatch, and separate SetIQ2XXSCooperative and SetIQ2XSCooperative controls. Scalar kernels remain callable as controls, fused ARM64 CPU remains the fallback unless a host cell independently clears its gate, and IQ2_S later joined the family lifecycle with its own parser and verdict.

body: PR #1234 CI proves Go 1.27 removed LoadFloat64x4Slice, LoadFloat32x8Slice, and StoreSlice, while LoadInt8x32 and LoadFloat32x8 now accept slices rather than array pointers. Darwin/ARM64 cannot compile these AMD64-only files, so local preflight missed the break. Replace only the renamed load/store calls and pointer adapters, preserve vector operation order and scalar fallbacks, remove now-unused unsafe imports, and add a local Linux/AMD64 GOEXPERIMENT=simd build/test gate to the validation record. Definition of done: GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GOEXPERIMENT=simd builds the full tree and compiles/runs internal/simd tests under Go 1.27.0; all PR checks then pass on the exact head.
